# The Ubuntu packages CI's jobs install, one pin a line (name=version), each from the cache entry
# .github/workflows/ci-caches.yaml's apt job fills on a push to main and installed by
# .github/scripts/apt-cache.sh with no network; that script's header says how. The fill, the
# install and the cache key's hashFiles all read this file, so moving a package to another version
# is one line here, and the next push to main fills an entry that holds it.
#
# Each version is the one these jobs ran with before this file existed, so no test reads another
# build than it did: in run 44533492400 daemon-go's step printed `tmux is already the newest version
# (3.4-1ubuntu0.2)` (the ubuntu-24.04 image carries it), and claude-envoy's and dispatch-ui's
# fetched zsh and zsh-common 5.9-6ubuntu2 from ports.ubuntu.com on ubuntu-24.04-arm;
# postgresql-client is the candidate `apt-cache policy` names in an ubuntu:24.04 container
# (2026-11-19), and ports.ubuntu.com's indexes hold the same three versions for arm64. Ubuntu's
# archive keeps only the newest version of a pocket: once noble-updates publishes a newer tmux,
# 3.4-1ubuntu0.2 is in no index, and a fill from an empty cache fails naming this pin. The entry
# already filled keeps installing it, since its key moves only with this file and the script;
# move the pin then.
#
# Who installs what (each job's step says why its tests need it):
#   tmux               daemon-go and pi-envoy; e2e.yaml's stage1-skeleton proof
#   zsh                claude-envoy and dispatch-ui; dispatch-unit-repeat.yaml's harness lane
#   postgresql-client  e2e.yaml's proofs whose row in .github/e2e-scripts.json names it
# e2e.yaml installs the words of a row's `apt` list, so each of them needs a line here.
#
# tmux 3.8, tmux's current release, whose JSON #{window_layout} pull request #4513 reads, is in no
# archive this runner reads: noble holds 3.4 alone (3.4-1build1, and 3.4-1ubuntu0.2 in
# noble-updates), and noble-backports holds none. Nor would a newer Ubuntu's .deb do: 26.04's
# archive holds 3.6a (3.6a-2ubuntu0.2), whose package needs libc6 2.42 where noble has 2.39. A 3.8
# for noble would have to be a package built for noble, from an apt source the fill and the miss
# then read; once such a source is in the runner's apt, the change is this one line.
tmux=3.4-1ubuntu0.2
zsh=5.9-6ubuntu2
postgresql-client=16+257build1.1
